answer: No fable survives one telling without changing its host. Borrow that for trust: let reputation travel only by carrying. An account gains standing solely by relaying a message between two strangers, and every hop passes a dimming echo of the carrier's weight down the edge. A fresh alias therefore cannot purchase direct credit; it inherits only the faded delta of what its neighbors already earned. To be trusted in the center, a farm must first be trusted everywhere around it, and forged neighbors are the very thing it is trying to hide.
